walkthroughs.body_html:
A limited company is its own legal person.

Owners (shareholders) have limited liability — they only risk the money they put in. Their house is safe. 🏠

Ltd — Private. Shares only sold to friends and family. Most small companies.

plc — Public. Shares trade on the stock market. Examples: Tesco plc, BP plc.

A share is one slice of the company.

If the company makes profit, shareholders may get a dividend — a cash payment per share.

More rules: companies must file accounts with the government. 📑

mcqs.q: What do McGregor's Theory X and Theory Y describe?
options: Limited liability means a business can only operate for a limited time.
Theory X is about working in a factory and Theory Y is about office work.
Two contrasting management assumptions: Theory X assumes workers dislike work and need control; Theory Y assumes workers can be self-motivated and seek responsibility.
Theory X and Theory Y are stages of business growth.

mcqs.q: How do stakeholder and shareholder interests overlap and conflict?
options: Shareholders are external and stakeholders are internal.

Shareholders are a subset of stakeholders. Their interests overlap (long-term success benefits all) but conflict on issues like dividends vs investment, wages vs profits, or short-term gains vs long-term sustainability.
Limited liability means a business can only operate for a limited time.
Stakeholders and shareholders always want the same thing.
Limited liability means a business can only operate for a limited time.
Limited liability means the company has limited debts it can take on.
Shareholders' personal assets are protected if the company fails — they can only lose the amount they invested, not their personal wealth.
Theory X and Theory Y are stages of business growth.
